pages.text: A SACCO is a member-owned savings and credit cooperative. Members contribute share capital and savings deposits and may borrow against their deposits. Annual dividends and interest on deposits are decided by the members at the general meeting. A deposit-taking SACCO is licensed and inspected by the authority. Members should read the annual report and attend the general meeting.

The SACCO Deposit Fund covers a member's deposits up to SYN Sh 250,000 per member. New members of a deposit-taking SACCO must hold minimum share capital of SYN Sh 5,000. This guide was issued by the SYN SACCO Societies Authority for retail investors and is reviewed every year. Readers who need advice on SACCOs should consult a licensed adviser, because this guide gives information only. [SYNTHETIC TEST DATA: fictional organisations and invented figures. Not real financial information.]
